title: Minimum proof skeleton suppresses unsupported bridge completion
target: human reconstruction of HF01 evidence boundaries
core_hypothesis: A small set of claim-conditioned proof barriers can reduce unsupported mental bridge completion while imposing less cognitive cost than a full explanatory ladder.

arms.endpoint_only: headline claim plus endpoint evidence, without mandatory proof-barrier display
arms.full_ladder: fixed detailed projection ladder exposing mechanism, probes, uncertainty, counterexamples and next evidence
arms.minimum_proof_skeleton: claim-conditioned SOURCE / TYPE / CEILING / REACHABILITY badges with optional detail hidden by default

adversarial_transfer_items: two datasets using one shared projection family -> two independent projection confirmations
primary_predictions: minimum_proof_skeleton time/stage exposure < full_ladder at equal or better claim-boundary accuracy
rejection_conditions: proof skeleton increases confidence without reducing false bridges
full ladder materially outperforms proof skeleton on transfer accuracy after burden is accounted for
participants bypass or ignore proof barriers so often that the nominal structure does not alter reconstruction
benefit appears only on verbatim recall and not on new inference items
analysis_discipline: freeze unsupported bridge items before participant exposure
report arm-wise burden and accuracy rather than a single composite score
do not treat comprehension improvement as evidence of hair biology change
claim_boundary: Passing HF-VAL-005 would support a human-interface/epistemic-control design. It would not validate any biological recovery pathway.
